name: Ploughshares Fund (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a nuclear war kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: Ploughshares Fund (San Francisco) funds and convenes the groups working to cut the risk of nuclear war: in the year to June 2025 it spent $7.6M, $3.1M of it in grants to 46 organisations (arms-control research and advocacy, diplomacy with Iran, North Korea and China, media, laboratory watchdogs) and $2.6M on its own coalitions, communications and the Nuclear Futures Fellowship; this model covers all of it. At the defaults it averts about 26 years of healthy life per $1,000, from 1.2 to 560 on the combined range: each dollar is valued as a typical project's cut in the forecast risk of nuclear war (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), a grant as a typical dollar of the grantee's work (no grantee has a model on the site yet), with deaths valued like every death and the future lost counted through the discount rate. It is more than ten times its peers because most of them work only on AI, and Rethink's typical nuclear project averts far more deaths per dollar than a typical AI project; it is close to the Nuclear Threat Initiative. The biggest uncertainty is how much a dollar of such work cuts the risk (Rethink calls its figures placeholders; the range runs ten times either way); the result also moves with the years a cut counts and the discount rate. Every branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Grants: share of the grant money aimed at nuclear-war risk
rows.explainer: Of the $3.0M: about $0.17M (Marshallese education, the Nuclear Truth Project, RECA advocacy, Kiribati delegates, Bombshelltoe) is justice for people harmed by past testing, which doesn't cut the risk (5.6%); about $0.5M (WASL's peacebuilding in South Asia and the Middle East, the Women of the Middle East Network, J Street, NIAC Action, Win Without War) is diplomacy and war prevention only partly about nuclear weapons, counted half (8%). 86% (75% to 95%), our judgment from the grant purposes in Schedule I.

rows.label: Grants: how far the typical project's effect applies to the nuclear work funded
rows.explainer: The grants fund typical field work: arms-control research and advocacy (the Arms Control Association, FAS, the Stimson Center, RAND, Carnegie), congressional advocacy (FCNL, Win Without War), Track 2 on Korea (the Quincy Institute, the National Committee on North Korea), media (Inkstick, ReThink Media) and watchdogs of the weapons laboratories. A funder choosing grantees in the field for 44 years may pick better than average; small advocacy and media grants have long paths to the risk. 0.8 (0.35 to 1.2), our judgment, as NTI's 0.8 for a mix of policy work and public education.

rows.label: Own work: share of the programmatic activity that runs the grantmaking
rows.explainer: Part of the $2,559,135 of programmatic activity is the cost of choosing, managing and reporting on 46 grants: the 990 puts no grant administration in management and general ($915,743, mostly investment fees, legal, accounting and finance staff), and the annual report's programme services are only grants and programmatic activity. Its output is the grants, already valued per dollar granted, so this share adds nothing of its own (its cost stays in the cost). 25% (10% to 40%), our judgment from the programme staff: of 23 employees, the programmes director and grants team against the field-building, coalition and communications staff; any value grant selection adds is in gr_evidence_adj.

rows.label: Own work: how far the typical project's effect applies to Ploughshares' coalitions, convening and communications
rows.explainer: Ploughshares' own work is coordination (the Stop the New Nuclear Arms Race Roundtable, the Iran coalition, the North Korea working group, Aligning Action, the March 2025 Hill day), communications (the Story Center's forty pieces, the narrative project with NTI) and the Women Transforming Global Security network: the longest paths to the risk, with no output taken up by governments named. 0.6 (0.25 to 1), our judgment, below the grants and NTI's 0.8.

rows.label: Fellowship: how far the typical project's effect applies to the fellows' work
rows.explainer: The fellows' added work is valued at a typical dollar of nuclear work (fb_deaths_per_million), so 1 unless their work differs: fellows from PSR, NTI, the Arms Control Association and similar groups do typical field work. 1 (0.7 to 1.2), our judgment, as GovAI's fellowship.

rows.label: Grants: share of the funded work other organisations would not have done now
rows.explainer: Whether the research, advocacy and education the grants pay for would have been done now by other groups in the field (other think tanks' arms-control analysis, other advocacy coalitions on the Hill, other Track 2 channels on Korea): the field is small and each grantee has its niche, but many overlap. 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9), our judgment, as NTI's counterfactual_adj for the same question; that the work would have come years later is in years_of_impact.

rows.label: Grants: share of the funded work the grantees' other funders would not have paid for
rows.explainer: Whether the grantees' other funders (Longview, Carnegie Corporation, the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, Open Society) would have paid for the work Ploughshares funded had it not: the field's money is shrinking (MacArthur left in 2021; annual report p. 44: "philanthropic support for nuclear threat reduction is declining sector-wide"), so most of it would go unfunded, but a large funder might fill a gap at an established grantee. 0.8 (0.6 to 0.95), our judgment. A question about the grant's own counterfactual, so it sits here; whether Ploughshares' own funders would fill a gap if a donor gave less is the room factor of @next_dollar.ploughshares_fund, and leverage_funging_adj stays 1 as in every catastrophic-risk model.

rows.label: Grants: share of the funded work that would not have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Two questions about the funded work, each its own row: other organisations doing it now (gr_cf_other_orgs) and the grantees' other funders paying for it (gr_cf_other_funders).

rows.label: Own work: share of Ploughshares' coordination no one else would have done now
rows.explainer: Whether others would have run the field's coordination now: few others run its coalitions (Ploughshares facilitates and resources them), though members would keep meeting without it. 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9), our judgment, as NTI's counterfactual_adj.

rows.label: Fellowship: share of the places no one else would have offered now
rows.explainer: Other nuclear fellowships exist (the Scoville fellowship, the Stanton fellowships, CSIS's Project on Nuclear Issues), but few for mid-career staff with a funded capstone. 0.8 (0.6 to 0.95), our judgment, below GovAI's 0.9 because the field has more fellowships for its size.

rows.label: Grants: Ploughshares' share of the resources behind the funded work
rows.explainer: A grant buys its own share of a grantee's work: the cut is per dollar, so co-funders' dollars are already left out; only volunteers' and partners' unpaid time inside the funded projects (the Physicists Coalition's scientists, faith groups) is not in the cost. 0.95 (0.8 to 1), our judgment.

rows.label: Own work: Ploughshares' share of the resources behind its coordination
rows.explainer: The coalitions and the Hill day run on partners' staff time Ploughshares doesn't pay for (about 30 people from more than 10 organisations on the Hill day, annual report p. 32), and the narrative project and Women Transforming Global Security are joint with NTI, The Elders and Horizon 2045. 0.6 (0.4 to 0.85), our judgment.

rows.label: Fellowship: Ploughshares' share of the resources behind the fellowship
rows.explainer: The fellowship is a joint venture with Horizon 2045, which shares its design and coaching; the fellows' employers give their time. 0.6 (0.4 to 0.8), our judgment.

rows.label: How far the typical project's effect applies to this charity's work
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only: the grants (their relevant share × gr_evidence_adj), Ploughshares' own work (less the share that runs the grantmaking, own_grant_admin_share) and the fellowship.
rows.formula: (w_gr * gr_relevant_share * gr_evidence_adj + w_own * (1 - own_grant_admin_share) * own_evidence_adj + w_fb * fb_evidence_adj) / (w_gr + w_own + w_fb)

rows.label: Share of the work no one else would have done now
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only (weighted by each branch's healthy years after its evidence step, so the product of the canonical rows is the sum over branches).
rows.formula: (w_gr * gr_relevant_share * gr_evidence_adj * gr_counterfactual_adj + w_own * (1 - own_grant_admin_share) * own_evidence_adj * own_counterfactual_adj + w_fb * fb_evidence_adj * fb_counterfactual_adj) / ((w_gr + w_own + w_fb) * evidence_adj)

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only (weighted after their evidence and counterfactual steps).
rows.formula: (w_gr * gr_relevant_share * gr_evidence_adj * gr_counterfactual_adj * gr_attribution_share_shared + w_own * (1 - own_grant_admin_share) * own_evidence_adj * own_counterfactual_adj * own_attribution_share_shared + w_fb * fb_evidence_adj * fb_counterfactual_adj * fb_attribution_share_shared) / ((w_gr + w_own + w_fb) * evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj)

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Whether other funders of nuclear work would give less if small donors gave more is the room factor of @next_dollar.ploughshares_fund (docs/normalization.md 2.10), so it isn't asked again here (one question per adjustment): 1, our judgment, as for every catastrophic-risk model; 0.85 to 1.05 for funging the room factor misses.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome of Ploughshares' or its grantees' work on the risk is measured; the cut per dollar is a typical project's from Rethink Priorities' model and the chances are forecasts, so the shared missing-data step applies (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the catastrophes counted, each part a share of the modelled value: work against a limited nuclear war or a single detonation (the testing and Korea work), which kills far fewer than 10% of people and has no shared forecast (nuclear_smaller_per_year 0), and grants against conventional war (diplomacy with Iran in the year of the June 2025 strikes), together 8%; the compensation and recognition won for people harmed by testing (the RECA expansion a grantee pushed for: a transfer within the US whose net gain after its cost to taxpayers is small), 2%; Ploughshares' influence on other funders' giving to the field (its president's talks at the Global Philanthropy Forum and Skoll World Forum in spring 2025, advice to donors; no money moved is published), 3% (0 to 10%). 13% (0 to 40%) in all, our judgment; NTI's model takes 10% for the first kind.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: A typical project's chance of backfiring is already in the shared cut per dollar (Rethink Priorities' backfire step). Ploughshares' grants fund policy, advocacy and education, which can't speed up any capability. 0, down to −5%, our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): advocacy for restraint and disarmament could, some argue, weaken deterrence or provoke a backlash, and alarming public messages can feed fatalism (the reason for Ploughshares' narrative work); none is shown to happen. 0, down to −5%, our judgment.
